points.text: RL framing is metaphor; method never computes V, r or TD error
Lower-variance and stability claims rest on one set of curves
TD vs MC confounds extra inputs; needs MC with same info and per-turn controls
Long-term planning claim never directly tested
RPO feedbacker receives user goal, API calls, expert feedback that baselines lack
'MC-style (TextGrad)' is the authors' reimplementation, not actual TextGrad
APO binary-label and GPO multi-turn adaptations described only briefly
No comparison with OPRO, Reflexion-style, ProTeGi, Agent-Pro or simple trajectory baseline
Candidates, epochs and LLM calls per baseline not stated; budget uncontrolled
+replay drives most gains while baselines get no history access
Tables lack variances, seeds or CIs; small gaps likely within noise
Size of sharded Spider subset not given in main text
Best-of-2 selection on validation risks selection bias; test separation unclear
Non-monotone entries like APO below baseline suggest variance, undiscussed
LLM-simulated user may be exploited; no human-user evaluation
Prompts not tested for transfer across domains, simulators or backbones
'Generalizes across agents' only partly shown; conflates optimizer vs system LLM
Small expert eval with combined preference; no agreement, breakdown or significance
Comparison to 7B Huatuo-GPT-II reflects stronger base model, not prompt optimization
Unclear whether evaluating experts are the same as feedback experts
TCM gains over plain system modest and not significant
Optimized prompts may add confident medical advice; safety unexamined
Medical QA arguably not a long-term planning task
No cost, token or latency numbers for optimization or inference
No empirical comparison to Reflexion-like self-refine methods at inference
Replay context grows with epochs; scaling and value of old entries undiscussed
Prompt length, evolution and learned strategies not analysed; only one example
Claims like robust, stable, efficient, lower-variance exceed evidence
Petrov et al. argument used post hoc to explain TCM results
Mean delta includes OracleFull and is dominated by low-baseline models
Code is not yet released
LLM feedback to adjust prompts already explored in Self-Refine and Reflexion
Unclear how choice of feedbacker and rewriter base models affects performance
Unclear epochs, interaction data and update timeliness needed in live systems
No formal definition relating RPO to states, actions and value functions
Quality of feedbacker and reasonableness of rewards not studied
No ablation replacing or analysing Feedbacker and Rewriter individually
No comparison with RL-based methods like StablePrompt
No quantitative API call or token comparison versus APO or GPO
High variance in Figure 4; tables lack standard deviations
Prompts used for generating text gradients insufficiently explained
Per-step feedback on long trajectories may be very expensive
What practitioners should do when feedback is not useful is unaddressed
No qualitative analysis of the generated feedback

Spider subset size not given

Simulated user and no human-user evaluation
No transfer tests across domains, simulators or backbones
Generalization claim conflates optimizer LLM and agent
Medical QA human evaluation weak
Huatuo-GPT-II comparison confounded by base model
Optimization and evaluation experts may overlap
TCM improvements modest and not significant
Safety of optimized medical prompts not examined
Medical QA is not a long-term planning task
Efficiency claim not measured
No inference-time comparison with self-refine methods
Replay context growth and scaling not discussed
No analysis of prompt evolution or what optimizer learns
Claims overstated
Post hoc explanation of TCM results
Mean relative gain metric misleading
Code not released

Effect of base model choice for feedbacker/rewriter unclear
No formal theoretical link to RL
Roles of feedbacker and rewriter not analysed or ablated
API call and token costs not quantified
No standard deviations despite high variance
Unclear handling when feedback is not useful
No qualitative analysis of generated feedback
